t.1.54.2: From her lowing were born the Kāmbojas, radiant as the sun, and then from her udder sprang forth the Pahlavas, weapons in hand.
t.1.54.1: Then, seeing them thrown into disarray and bewildered by Viśvāmitra's weapons, Vasiṣṭha urged her on: "O wish-granting cow, create more through your yogic power!"
t.1.54.3: From the region of her womb came forth the Yavana, and likewise from the region of her dung the Śakas; and from the pores of her hair came the Mlecchas and the Harītas, together with the Kirātas.
t.1.54.4: By them, O Raghunandana, the army of Viśvāmitra was destroyed in that very instant, together with its foot soldiers and elephants, its horses and its chariots.
t.1.54.5: But the hundred sons of Viśvāmitra, bearing weapons of many kinds, saw the army destroyed by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.54.7: Then the sons of Viśvāmitra, together with their horses, chariots and foot-soldiers, were reduced to ashes in an instant by the great-souled Vasiṣṭha.
t.1.54.6: He rushed at the furious Vasiṣṭha, foremost among those who murmur prayers, but with a mere cry of “huṃ” the great sage burned them all to ashes.
t.1.54.8: Seeing his sons and his army destroyed, the greatly renowned Viśvāmitra then became ashamed and was overcome with anxious thought.
t.1.54.10: His sons and his army slain, wretched like a bird whose wings have been clipped, his pride crushed and his zeal destroyed, he fell into despondency.
t.1.54.9: Like an ocean stilled of its surge, like a serpent whose fangs have been broken, like the sun in eclipse, he at once was bereft of all his splendour.
t.1.54.11: Appointing his one son to the kingdom with the charge, "Protect the earth in accordance with the dharma of a kṣatriya," he then went forth to the forest.
t.1.54.12: Having gone to the slope of the Himavant, frequented by Kiṃnaras and Uragas, he of great austerity performed austerities to win the favor of Mahādeva.
t.1.54.13: Then, after some time, the lord of the gods, the bestower of boons whose banner bears the bull, revealed himself to the great sage Viśvāmitra.
t.1.54.15: Thus addressed by the god, Viśvāmitra of great austerity bowed down before Mahādeva and spoke these words.
t.1.54.14: For what purpose are you performing austerities, O king? Tell me what you wish to say. I am a giver of boons; let the boon you desire be named.
t.1.54.16: If you are pleased with me, O Mahādeva, O sinless one, let the Dhanurveda be granted to me, together with its aṅgas, upāṅgas and upaniṣads, and with all its secrets.
t.1.54.18: "By your grace, O God of gods, may what I desire come to pass." Saying the words "So be it," the Lord of the gods went to heaven.
t.1.54.17: O sinless one, may all the weapons that exist among the gods, the Dānavas, the great sages, the Gandharvas, Yakṣas and Rakṣases become manifest to me.
t.1.54.19: Having obtained the weapons, the mighty royal sage Viśvāmitra, possessed of great pride, then became filled with arrogance.
t.1.54.20: Swelling with might like the ocean at the full moon, he then deemed Vasiṣṭha, the best of sages, as good as slain.
t.1.54.21: Then the king went to the hermitage and released his missiles, by which that entire ascetic grove was burnt down through the blazing power of those weapons.
t.1.54.22: Seeing that weapon of the wise Viśvāmitra being launched, the sages, terrified, fled by the hundreds in all directions.
t.1.54.23: Those who were disciples of Vasiṣṭha, and likewise the beasts and birds, terrified with fear, fled by the thousands in every direction.
t.1.54.24: The hermitage of the great-souled Vasiṣṭha became empty; for a moment it was utterly silent, like a barren wasteland.
t.1.54.25: As Vasiṣṭha kept saying again and again, "Do not be afraid! Today I shall destroy the son of Gādhi, as the sun destroys the mist."
t.1.54.26: Having spoken thus, the greatly radiant Vasiṣṭha, foremost among those who recite prayers, then angrily addressed these words to Viśvāmitra.
t.1.54.28: Having spoken thus, greatly enraged, like the smokeless fire of universal destruction, he swiftly raised his staff, which was like a second staff of Yama.
t.1.54.27: Since you have destroyed this hermitage that flourished over so long a time, and since you are wicked, O fool, you shall therefore cease to exist.
